issues.description: No regression test ships with the bug fix to lock in new behavior.
issues.detail: The commit claims to fix state reuse, stack cleanup, and yield ordering, but the diff carries no test that fails on the parent commit and passes here. A table-driven test that Sorts twice on the same Sorter with overlapping keys, plus one exercising early `return false` from yield, would pin the new contract. For a bug fix in topological sort, landing on faith is not acceptable.

issues.description: Collapsing `working` into `walking` changes cycle-detection semantics without an explicit invariant.
issues.detail: The two states tracked distinct moments: `working` meant children being expanded, `walking` meant on-stack awaiting second visit. Folding them means push()'s cycle-detection branch now fires for any node on the current DFS path, including before its children are pushed. Likely correct, but the loop invariant (walking == on-stack-and-not-yet-emitted) should be stated at the const block before merging.

issues.description: Deferred cleanup runs only on iterator exit, not on Sort() entry.
issues.detail: The defer that clears state and stack lives inside the returned yield closure, so it fires only when the caller iterates or aborts. A caller who calls Sort() to obtain the iter.Seq but never iterates leaves prior state dirty. The reuse contract should be named explicitly, and reset should also happen at the top of Sort, not only on iterator exit.

issues.description: Moving `state[k] = sorted` inside the yield success branch is a semantic fix buried in cleanup.
issues.detail: Previously every popped node was marked sorted unconditionally; now only nodes that actually yielded are. An abandoned iteration no longer marks the node sorted, which is the real bug fix. The commit message buries this among cleanup bullets, and the invariant `pop implies sorted` is now conditional. Call it out explicitly in the message or restore the unconditional write.

issues.description: Typos in the load-bearing comment that now serves as the state-machine spec.
issues.detail: The rewritten comment contains `visisted` and `if its the first` (missing apostrophe). This is the prose that explains the entire two-visit DFS trick and is now the de facto spec for the state machine. Cheap to fix; worth fixing because the surrounding code holds a higher bar.

issues.description: Three logical changes bundled into one patch make future bisection harder.
issues.detail: The diff combines (1) collapsing `working` into `walking`, (2) moving cleanup into a defer with clear(stack), and (3) reordering so `sorted` is set only after a successful yield. Each is defensible individually; together they obscure which change caused any future regression. Split next time.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the patch is on the right track but under-audited. Three semantic changes (state collapse, deferred cleanup, yield-conditional sorted-marking) ship bundled with no regression test, and the loop invariant carrying the fix is never stated. The deferred cleanup is scoped to iterator exit rather than Sort() entry, leaving a hole if callers obtain the iter.Seq without consuming it. Comment typos in the now-load-bearing spec and a missing commit-message callout for the yield-ordering fix round out the cleanup needed before merge.
